f.title: EMA keeps identifiable personal data no longer than necessary for the purpose
f.statement: Personal data processed by a Union institution or body must be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes of the processing. They may be stored for longer periods insofar as they will be processed solely for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with Article 13, subject to appropriate technical and organisational measures to safeguard the rights and freedoms of the data subject.
f.applicability: Processing of personal data by EMA as a Union body controller, including EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance data; relevant to MAHs exchanging personal data with EMA.
f.exceptions: Longer storage solely for archiving in the public interest, research or statistical purposes under Art. 13, with safeguards.

f.title: EMA processes personal data on the basis of a public-interest task or a legal obligation laid down in Union law
f.statement: Processing by a Union institution or body is lawful only if and to the extent that at least one ground in Article 5(1) applies, including that processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the Union institution or body, or for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject.
f.applicability: EMA processing of personal data in EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance activities (Art. 5(2): the basis for points (a) and (b) must be laid down in Union law).

rows.actor: European Medicines Agency (EMA) as controller (Union body)
rows.review_note: Review: quote covers points (a)-(b); the "only if" chapeau and Art. 5(2) are summarised from the same article. Double-check: chapeau outside the quote, so 89.

f.title: Recipients in the Union (e.g. MAHs, national authorities) must establish that the personal data they receive from EMA are necessary
f.statement: Without prejudice to Articles 4 to 6 and 10, personal data may only be transmitted by a Union institution or body to recipients established in the Union other than Union institutions and bodies if: (a) the recipient establishes that the data are necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the recipient; or (b) the recipient establishes that transmission is necessary for a specific purpose in the public interest and the controller, where there is any reason to assume that the data subject's legitimate interests might be prejudiced, establishes that transmission is proportionate after demonstrably weighing the competing interests.
f.clause: Art. 9(1) Transmissions to recipients in the Union other than Union bodies
f.applicability: Requests by EU-established recipients, such as MAHs or national competent authorities, for personal data held by EMA (e.g. ICSR data beyond the access granted under the EudraVigilance access policy).

rows.actor: EMA as transmitting controller; recipient established in the Union (e.g. national competent authority or MAH requesting data from EMA)
rows.quote:
Without prejudice to Articles 4 to 6 and 10, personal data shall only be transmitted to recipients established in the Union other than Union institutions and bodies if:
(a)
the recipient establishes that the data are necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the recipient; or
(b)
the recipient establishes that it is necessary to have the data transmitted for a specific purpose in the public interest and the controller, where there is any reason to assume that the data subject’s legitimate interests might be prejudiced, establishes that it is proportionate to transmit the personal data for that specific purpose after having demonstrably weighed the various competing interests.
rows.location: Art. 9(1) Transmissions to recipients in the Union other than Union bodies

f.title: Where EMA initiates a transmission, it must demonstrate that it is necessary and proportionate
f.statement: Where the controller initiates the transmission under Article 9, it must demonstrate that the transmission of personal data is necessary for and proportionate to the purposes of the transmission by applying the criteria in Article 9(1)(a) or (b).
f.clause: Art. 9(2) Transmission initiated by the controller
f.applicability: Processing of personal data by EMA as a Union body controller, including EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance data; relevant to MAHs exchanging personal data with EMA.

f.title: EMA processes health data under the public-health condition: quality and safety of medicinal products, on the basis of Union law
f.statement: Processing of special categories of personal data, including data concerning health, is prohibited unless an Article 10(2) condition applies. Under point (i), the prohibition does not apply where processing is necessary for reasons of public interest in the area of public health, such as protecting against serious cross-border threats to health or ensuring high standards of quality and safety of healthcare and of medicinal products or medical devices, on the basis of Union law which provides for suitable and specific measures to safeguard the rights and freedoms of the data subject, in particular professional secrecy.
f.clause: Art. 10(1)-(2)(i) Processing of special categories of personal data
f.applicability: EMA processing of patient health data in EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance activities.

rows.actor: European Medicines Agency (EMA) as controller (Union body)

rows.location: Art. 10(1)-(2)(i) Processing of special categories of personal data

f.title: EMA responds to data subject rights requests within one month of receipt
f.statement: The controller must provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 17 to 24 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request.
f.clause: Art. 14(3) Response time for data subject requests
f.applicability: Data subject requests concerning personal data held by EMA (e.g. in EudraVigilance); MAHs redirecting such requests should know EMA's clock.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: EMA may extend the response period by two further months for complex or numerous requests
f.statement: The one-month response period may be extended by two further months where necessary, taking into account the complexity and number of the requests.

f.applicability: Processing of personal data by EMA as a Union body controller, including EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance data; relevant to MAHs exchanging personal data with EMA.

f.title: If EMA does not act on a request, it tells the data subject why within one month, with the EDPS complaint option
f.statement: If the controller does not take action on the data subject's request, it must inform the data subject without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request of the reasons and of the possibility of lodging a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor and seeking a judicial remedy.
f.clause: Art. 14(4) Refusal to act on a request
f.applicability: Processing of personal data by EMA as a Union body controller, including EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance data; relevant to MAHs exchanging personal data with EMA.

f.title: EMA notifies a personal data breach to the EDPS without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of awareness
f.statement: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller must notify it to the European Data Protection Supervisor without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
f.clause: Art. 34(1) Notification of a personal data breach to the EDPS
f.applicability: Breaches of personal data held by EMA as controller (e.g. EudraVigilance); a breach on the MAH side is notified by the MAH under GDPR Art. 33.
f.exceptions: Not required where the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Quality system & CAPA

f.statement: The controller must inform the data protection officer about the personal data breach, and must document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts, their effects and the remedial action taken, so that the European Data Protection Supervisor can verify compliance with Article 34.
f.clause: Art. 34(5)-(6) DPO information and documentation of breaches

f.title: EMA communicates a high-risk personal data breach to the affected data subjects without undue delay
f.statement: When a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller must communicate the breach to the data subject without undue delay. The communication must describe in clear and plain language the nature of the breach and contain at least the information and measures referred to in points (b), (c) and (d) of Article 34(3).
f.clause: Art. 35(1) Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
f.applicability: Processing of personal data by EMA as a Union body controller, including EudraVigilance and other pharmacovigilance data; relevant to MAHs exchanging personal data with EMA.
f.exceptions: Not required where the Art. 35(3) conditions are met (protection measures such as encryption, subsequent measures removing the high risk, or disproportionate effort, in which case a public communication is made).
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Quality system & CAPA

dates.title: EUDPR (Regulation (EU) 2018/1725): enters into force
dates.scope: Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, including EMA, as controllers (Eurojust processing applies only from 12 December 2019 under Art. 101(2), not recorded)
dates.quote: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
dates.location: Article 101(1) Entry into force and application
dates.timing_note: Published in the Official Journal on 2018-11-21 (OJ L 295/39, header date 21.11.2018). Twentieth day following publication: 2018-11-21 + 20 days = 2018-12-11. Art. 101 states no separate general application date, so entry into force is the date from which EMA must apply it. The Eurojust-specific date (12 December 2019) is not relevant to EMA and is not recorded.
